claims.text: The conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is single phase.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The baseline alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Under dynamic adiabatic loading, the baseline alloy exhibits limited strain hardening.
Under dynamic adiabatic loading, the baseline alloy exhibits poor uniform deformability.
Under dynamic adiabatic loading, the baseline alloy fails rapidly.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of 1–2 vol% Y2O3 in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Nanoscale oxide particles impede dislocation motion in the alloy matrix.
Nanoscale oxide particles provide sites for heterogeneous deformation.
The oxide dispersion promotes a higher work-hardening response.
The oxide-induced work-hardening response delays strain localization.
Oxide dispersoids can activate deformation twinning during rapid deformation.
Oxide dispersoids can produce controlled dislocation pile-ups during rapid deformation.
A higher obstacle density and strain-hardening rate delay adiabatic shear-band formation.
Delayed shear-band formation reduces the rate of impact-induced energy release.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic compression, oxide dispersion will increase dynamic yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the baseline.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic compression, oxide dispersion will increase dynamic compressive strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the baseline.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic compression, the oxide-dispersed alloy will exhibit greater uniform deformability and localization resistance than the baseline.
At approximately 10^3 s^-1 under adiabatic compression, the oxide-dispersed alloy will fail later and release impact energy more slowly than the baseline.
